# mt-eval command reference

`mt-eval` is the evaluation harness. It runs a translation method over a set of
sentences, scores what came back, and keeps the record of the run (its run card).
The same pipeline translates source-only input (`translate`) and serves a method
behind the `/translate` contract (`serve`). It also drives sealed contests
(`contest`, `node`, `shared-task`) and the Join-a-project lane (`project`).

Install it with `python3 -m pip install mt-eval-harness` (Python 3.11 or newer).
Every command below prints its own help with `--help`.

This page is generated from the harness's own argument parser, so every command
and flag on it exists exactly as written.


## Global flags

These work before or after any subcommand, at any depth (`mt-eval --json test run.json` and `mt-eval test run.json --json` are the same).

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--non-interactive` | Never enter the guided selector, even on a TTY. Fail with a clear error if a corpus wasn't given. For scripts/agents. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON for structured output and errors (for agents / CI). Suppresses the guided interactive selector. |
| `--version` | Show the harness version and exit. |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show the help for `mt-eval` or for any subcommand, and exit. |

Option names are never abbreviated: `--mod` does not mean `--model`.

`mt-eval` with no subcommand runs [`mt-eval run`](#mt-eval-run) and takes the same options.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`mt-eval card`](#mt-eval-card) | Pretty-print a human-readable run card |
| [`mt-eval run`](#mt-eval-run) | Execute a translation run |
| [`mt-eval translate`](#mt-eval-translate) | Translate source-only input with a method — the run pipeline with nothing to score (deployment) |
| [`mt-eval serve`](#mt-eval-serve) | Serve a method that runs here behind the champollion /translate contract (deployment as a service; nothing scored) |
| [`mt-eval test`](#mt-eval-test) | Analyze a completed run log |
| [`mt-eval compare`](#mt-eval-compare) | Compare two or more runs |
| [`mt-eval dashboard`](#mt-eval-dashboard) | Generate interactive HTML dashboard |
| [`mt-eval list`](#mt-eval-list) | List available models, prompts, datasets |
| [`mt-eval corpora`](#mt-eval-corpora) | List eval corpora for a language pair (X→Y), or for one side |
| [`mt-eval recommend`](#mt-eval-recommend) | Method guidance for a language pair — availability + cited evidence |
| [`mt-eval queue`](#mt-eval-queue) | Run the top of the community compute queue with your own key |
| [`mt-eval publish`](#mt-eval-publish) | Submit a TestReport to the leaderboard |
| [`mt-eval contest`](#mt-eval-contest) | Sovereign contests: qualify locally, submit a model or method, rank, close |
| [`mt-eval node`](#mt-eval-node) | Organizer scoring node: poll intake, gate on the public qualifier, authorize per contest policy, score against organizer-held secret refs, publish scores-only — champollion.dev/docs/network/sovereignty/sovereign-eval-node |
| [`mt-eval shared-task`](#mt-eval-shared-task) | Multi-pair shared-task edition umbrella: one row groups the N per-pair contests of an AmericasNLP-style edition and carries its policy defaults — champollion.dev/docs/network/sovereignty/run-a-sovereign-contest. Grouping + defaults only — every gate stays per-contest |
| [`mt-eval logout`](#mt-eval-logout) | Remove stored authentication credentials |

| [`mt-eval export`](#mt-eval-export) | Package a TestReport as a champollion method plugin |
| [`mt-eval generate-plugin`](#mt-eval-generate-plugin) | Alias for 'export' — package a TestReport as a champollion method plugin |
| [`mt-eval export-config`](#mt-eval-export-config) | Generate a champollion.config.json snippet from a TestReport |
| [`mt-eval project`](#mt-eval-project) | Join a project: register yours, list them, offer files, accept offers |

## `mt-eval card`

Pretty-print a human-readable run card

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `log_paths …` | Run log JSON file(s) to render. Each one's report is found beside it (&lt;log>_report.json) or where `mt-eval test -o` recorded it in the log; a report file is read with the run log it records. A run with no report shows NOT SCORED and why. |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--report` | `PATH` |  | The report to show for the ONE run log given (a report written with `mt-eval test -o` before the log recorded its path). It must be that run's report. |

## `mt-eval run`

Execute a translation run

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--corpus` | `CORPUS` |  | Path to corpus file (.json, .jsonl, or .tsv). For parallel text files (FLORES+, WMT, NTREX), use --source-file and --reference-file instead. |
| `--source-file` | `SOURCE_FILE` |  | Path to source text file (one sentence per line). Use with --reference-file for parallel text corpora. |
| `--reference-file` | `REFERENCE_FILE` |  | Path to reference text file (aligned by line number). Use with --source-file for parallel text corpora. |
| `-d`, `--dataset` | `DATASET` | `all` | Dataset filter. Options: 'all', segment name, ID range ('0-61'), or single ID. Default: all |
| `--ids` | `IDS` |  | Comma-separated entry IDs to evaluate (overrides --dataset) |
| `--source-field` | `SOURCE_FIELD` | `source` | Field name for source text in corpus. Default: source |
| `--target-field` | `TARGET_FIELD` | `reference` | Field name for reference translation in corpus. Default: reference |
| `--source-lang` | `SOURCE_LANG` |  | Source language name (auto-detected from config if empty) |
| `--target-lang` | `TARGET_LANG` |  | Target language name (used in prompt). e.g. 'Plains Cree (nêhiyawêwin, SRO)' |
| `-m`, `--model` | `MODEL` | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | Exact model slug — the full OpenRouter id (google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview), or a direct provider's own exact name — or a comma-separated list of them for parallel multi-model runs. Default: google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview. No aliases and no floating ids (~vendor/…, …-latest): they are refused, naming the slug to write. With `--method local-model`, pass a Hugging Face id (facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M) or a transformers or CTranslate2 model directory here to run it locally — required: local-model has no default model, and the run records the model that loaded (a directory with a sha256 over its files). With `--method <plugin dir>`, the model is handed to the plugin as config.method_model, in the plugin's own naming, and recorded on the run card and in its fingerprint. |
| `--allow-model-pair-mismatch` | switch |  | With `--method local-model`: run an OPUS-MT pair model whose id names another language pair than the corpus's (opus-mt-en-fi on an eng>sme corpus, as a related-language baseline). Refused without this flag, because a pair model writes its own target language; the run card records the mismatch. |
| `--max-tokens` | `MAX_TOKENS` | `32768` | Max tokens per API call. Default: 32768 (generous headroom — translation outputs are short, unused tokens cost nothing). |
| `--provider` | one of: `openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `local`, `openai-compatible` | `openrouter` | LLM API provider. 'openrouter' (default) proxies any model. Direct providers call vendor APIs without a proxy. 'local' (alias 'openai-compatible') targets an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Groq, Together. It finds its server at, most specific first: --base-url, the LOCAL_API_BASE env var, OPENAI_API_BASE, OPENAI_BASE_URL, then Ollama's default http://localhost:11434/v1. |
| `--base-url` | `BASE_URL` |  | Override the provider's API endpoint (OpenAI-compatible base_url, e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama, https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 for Groq). Applies to --provider openai/local. Precedence: flag > env (--provider local: LOCAL_API_BASE, then OPENAI_API_BASE / OPENAI_BASE_URL; --provider openai: OPENAI_API_BASE) > default. |
| `--tools` | switch |  | Enable tool-calling (batch_size auto-overrides to 1) |
| `--tools-list` | `TOOLS_LIST` |  | Comma-separated tool names (requires --tools) |
| `--max-tool-rounds` | `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` | `8` | Max tool-calling rounds per entry. Default: 8 |
| `--no-cache` | switch |  | Disable caching (re-run all entries). NOT recommended. |
| `--cache-dir` | `CACHE_DIR` | `eval/cache/harness` | Cache directory. Default: eval/cache/harness |
| `--fuse` | switch |  | Also compute the FUSE-style comparator (reported separately, never in the chrF++ headline; an untrained reimplementation of the AmericasNLP-2025 FUSE approach). Needs the `fuse` extra: python3 -m pip install 'mt-eval-harness[fuse]'. Off by default — LaBSE is heavy. |
| `--metricx` | switch |  | Also compute MetricX-24 (Google, Apache-2.0) — the WMT24 Metrics shared-task winner and the metric WMT24++/TranslateGemma report against. A LOWER-IS-BETTER neural error metric (0–25), reported separately, NEVER in the chrF++ headline. Needs the `metricx` extra (python3 -m pip install 'mt-eval-harness[metricx]' plus the model code: python3 -m pip install git+https://github.com/google-research/metricx). Off by default — the mT5 backbone is heavy. |
| `--metricx-model` | `METRICX_MODEL` |  | Override the MetricX checkpoint (default: google/metricx-24-hybrid-large-v2p6). Pass an xl/xxl checkpoint for higher correlation, or a google/metricx-25-\* checkpoint for the newer generation. |
| `-b`, `--batch-size` | `BATCH_SIZE` | `25` | Entries per API call. Default: 25 (25× fewer API calls than batch_size=1). Auto-overrides to 1 when --tools is set. |
| `-c`, `--concurrency` | `CONCURRENCY` | `8` | Parallel API calls per model. Default: 8. For multi-model parallelism, pass multiple models with -m. |
| `-p`, `--prompt` | `PROMPT` | `naive` | System prompt version. Built-in: naive, custom. Use --coaching-file for custom coaching prompts. Default: naive |
| `--coaching-file` | `COACHING_FILE` |  | Path to a coaching file — Markdown, plain text or JSON; its full text is sent verbatim as the system prompt. Without --glossary, a JSON file's "dictionary" object ({"source term": "translation" or ["accepted", "forms"]}) is also the glossary terminology adherence is scored against (the scoring spec's coached-vocabulary rule). The text is recorded in the run card for reproducibility, and the run's condition is labelled 'coached' unless --prompt is set explicitly. |
| `--gates` | `FILE` |  | A gate-chain/1 file: checks applied to every translated segment before it is scored (run) or written (translate) — thresholds on a metric plugin's per-segment value, e.g. an FST validity check. The headline scores what ships; the ungated score and the refusal rate are reported beside it. |
| `--deployment` | `FILE` |  | A deployment/1 file (deploy/&lt;name>.json): its method, model, gates and target script — the same file `mt-eval serve --deployment` serves, so what is measured is what ships. Not given with --method, -m, --gates or --target-script; the corpus must be in the deployment's pair. |
| `--glossary` | `GLOSSARY` |  | Evaluation glossary for terminology adherence: a JSON file, {"source term": "translation" or ["accepted", "forms"]} (or an object with that under "dictionary"). A scoring input only — never sent to the model. Give every run you compare the same file, so their terminology scores mean the same thing. Takes precedence over a coaching file's dictionary. |
| `--coaching` | `COACHING` |  | Inline coaching text (for short prompts). Mutually exclusive with --coaching-file. |
| `--style-profile` | `STYLE_PROFILE` |  | Path to a style profile JSON for brand voice analysis. Enables writing style consistency metrics (a diagnostic, never in the headline). See docs for format. |
| `-o`, `--output-dir` | `OUTPUT_DIR` | `eval/logs/harness` | Output directory for RunLog. Default: eval/logs/harness |
| `-n`, `--name` | `NAME` |  | Human-readable run name (appended to run ID) |
| `--temperature` | `TEMPERATURE` | `0.0` | Sampling temperature. Default: 0.0 (shared/model-defaults.json — what is measured is what ships) |
| `--dry-run` | switch |  | Validate config without making API calls |
| `--max-cost` | `USD` |  | Abort before translation starts if the pre-spend cost estimate exceeds this cap (USD). An UNKNOWN estimate (un-priceable model, MT engine, method plugin) also aborts — unknown ≠ free. Default: no cap. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | switch |  | Skip confirmation prompts (e.g. accept the upstream data license when a missing corpus is fetched from source). Required for non-interactive/CI runs that trigger a fetch. |
| `--publish` | switch |  | After a successful run, publish the scored report to the leaderboard without prompting — the one-step equivalent of running, then `mt-eval publish <report>`. Honors the same content-safety gating as `mt-eval publish` (NC / held-out / unregistered corpora publish scores only). Requires sign-in (or --anonymous), and --prod for the live leaderboard. |
| `--prod`, `--yes-prod` | switch |  | With --publish: explicitly authorize the write to the PRODUCTION leaderboard (same switch as `mt-eval publish --prod`; or set MT_EVAL_ALLOW_PROD=1). Without it a prod publish is refused. |
| `--anonymous` | switch |  | With --publish: publish without signing in (submitter shown as 'anonymous'; rate-limited per IP; same integrity gates). |
| `--attest-no-training` | switch |  | Record a contamination self-attestation: that the method/model under evaluation was NOT trained on this corpus. The guided (interactive) run asks for this; agents/scripts pass this flag. |
| `--allow-data-collection` | switch |  | Lift the privacy-preserving transmission default for an UNREGISTERED corpus you hold the rights to. By default any corpus without a redistribution-cleared license is routed only through no-train channels (OpenRouter provider routing pinned to data_collection=deny). Has no effect on registered restricted corpora (NC / held-out / quarantined) — their channel rule can never be lifted. |
| `--attest-local-transport` | switch |  | For a consent-required or sealed corpus run through an EXTERNAL method plugin: attest that the method's transport is fully local (nothing reaches a remote model API). Recorded in the RunLog. Without this, such runs refuse — remote evaluation of consent-required corpora needs the rights-holder's recorded permission — champollion.dev/docs/agents/data-rules. |
| `--accept-terms` | switch |  | Acknowledge a gated dataset's terms non-interactively (you have accepted them upstream and set the token, e.g. HF_TOKEN). The fetch still fails honestly if the token is missing or terms aren't accepted on your account. |
| `--accept-nc-terms` | switch |  | Acknowledge a NON-COMMERCIAL (CC-BY-NC / -NC-SA) corpus's terms: that you will use it (and the results) for non-commercial / research purposes only and will not redistribute its content. Required to run against an NC corpus. The guided (interactive) run asks for this; agents/scripts pass this flag. Distinct from --accept-terms (which covers gated-dataset access). |
| `--method-card` | `METHOD_CARD` |  | Path to a method card JSON file (see docs/method-card-spec.md). Embeds the method description in the run card for leaderboard display. |
| `--method` | `METHOD` |  | A self-contained MT system name (amazon-translate, apertium, deepl, google-translate, lexicon, libretranslate, local-model, microsoft-translator, tilde, translated) OR a path to a method plugin directory (method.json + Python module). When set, the harness delegates translation to it; prompt and tool flags are ignored. `local-model` runs the model given with -m on this machine; `lexicon` looks each word up in the dictionary given with -m (a .tsv source&lt;TAB>target) — the floor a trained model has to beat. |
| `--source-code` | `SOURCE_CODE` |  | ISO source language code for MT systems (e.g. 'en'). Overrides the code auto-detected from the corpus language_pair. |
| `--target-lang-code`, `--target-code` | `TARGET_LANG_CODE` |  | The target language's code (BCP-47 / ISO 639, e.g. 'fr', 'de', 'crk'). It overrides the code the corpus declares: the prompt names the language from its card, the eval standard (FST, metrics) is chosen for it, and MT systems are sent it. --target-code is an alias. |
| `--target-script` | `ISO15924` |  | The script the translations must be written in, as an ISO 15924 code (e.g. Latn, Cans) — one the target's language card lists. The harness's prompt asks for it (appended to a coaching file's text too). For a language written in more than one script, use the script your references are in; without it the model picks. Not for an MT engine or method plugin (they get no prompt). |
| `--skip-fst` | switch |  | Score without FST acceptance, even if an FST is available for the target language; the run card marks it not computed. Without this flag a missing FST stops the run before translation and names the command that installs it (`mt-eval setup --lang <code>`) — run installs nothing. |
| `--skip-eval-standard` | switch |  | Score without the language card's eval-standard metrics (an external package, e.g. the Plains Cree standard); the run card marks them not computed. Without this flag a missing package stops the run before translation and names the pip install the card declares — run installs nothing. |

| `--attest-no-training` | switch |  | Record a contamination self-attestation: that the method/model under evaluation was NOT trained on this corpus. The guided (interactive) run asks for this; agents/scripts pass this flag. |
| `--allow-data-collection` | switch |  | Lift the privacy-preserving transmission default for an UNREGISTERED corpus you hold the rights to. By default any corpus without a redistribution-cleared license is routed only through no-train channels (OpenRouter provider routing pinned to data_collection=deny). Has no effect on registered restricted corpora (NC / held-out / quarantined) — their channel rule can never be lifted. |
| `--attest-local-transport` | switch |  | For a consent-required or sealed corpus run through an EXTERNAL method plugin: attest that the method's transport is fully local (nothing reaches a remote model API). Recorded in the RunLog. Without this, such runs refuse — remote evaluation of consent-required corpora needs the rights-holder's recorded permission — champollion.dev/docs/agents/data-rules. |
| `--accept-terms` | switch |  | Acknowledge a gated dataset's terms non-interactively (you have accepted them upstream and set the token, e.g. HF_TOKEN). The fetch still fails honestly if the token is missing or terms aren't accepted on your account. |
| `--accept-nc-terms` | switch |  | Acknowledge a NON-COMMERCIAL (CC-BY-NC / -NC-SA) corpus's terms: that you will use it (and the results) for non-commercial / research purposes only and will not redistribute its content. Required to run against an NC corpus. The guided (interactive) run asks for this; agents/scripts pass this flag. Distinct from --accept-terms (which covers gated-dataset access). |
| `--method-card` | `METHOD_CARD` |  | Path to a method card JSON file (see docs/method-card-spec.md). Embeds the method description in the run card for leaderboard display. |
| `--method` | `METHOD` |  | A self-contained MT system name (amazon-translate, apertium, deepl, google-translate, lexicon, libretranslate, local-model, microsoft-translator, tilde, translated) OR a path to a method plugin directory (method.json + Python module). When set, the harness delegates translation to it; prompt and tool flags are ignored. `local-model` runs the model given with -m on this machine; `lexicon` looks each word up in the dictionary given with -m (a .tsv source&lt;TAB>target) — the floor a trained model has to beat. |
| `--source-code` | `SOURCE_CODE` |  | ISO source language code for MT systems (e.g. 'en'). Overrides the code auto-detected from the corpus language_pair. |
| `--target-lang-code`, `--target-code` | `TARGET_LANG_CODE` |  | The target language's code (BCP-47 / ISO 639, e.g. 'fr', 'de', 'crk'). It overrides the code the corpus declares: the prompt names the language from its card, the eval standard (FST, metrics) is chosen for it, and MT systems are sent it. --target-code is an alias. |
| `--target-script` | `ISO15924` |  | The script the translations must be written in, as an ISO 15924 code (e.g. Latn, Cans) — one the target's language card lists. The harness's prompt asks for it (appended to a coaching file's text too). For a language written in more than one script, use the script your references are in; without it the model picks. Not for an MT engine or method plugin (they get no prompt). |
| `--skip-fst` | switch |  | Score without FST acceptance, even if an FST is available for the target language; the run card marks it not computed. Without this flag a missing FST stops the run before translation and names the command that installs it (`mt-eval setup --lang <code>`) — run installs nothing. |
| `--skip-eval-standard` | switch |  | Score without the language card's eval-standard metrics (an external package, e.g. the Plains Cree standard); the run card marks them not computed. Without this flag a missing package stops the run before translation and names the pip install the card declares — run installs nothing. |
| `--out` | `FILE` |  | Where the translations go: .jsonl ({id, source, output}) or .tsv (source&lt;TAB>output). Default: &lt;run id>.translations.jsonl beside the run log. It carries the input's terms (and a lexicon run's dictionary's, or the model's) as a set/1 sidecar. A method whose output is local-only (a model trained on local-only sentences, a dictionary marked local-only) writes it only inside the project unless --holders-agreed-by |
| `--holders-agreed-by` | `WHO` |  | for a method whose output is local-only, written outside the project (--out or -o): who among the data's holders agreed that it may be written there (recorded in the file's sidecar; the file stays marked local-only) |

## `mt-eval serve`

Serve a method that runs here behind the champollion /translate contract (deployment as a service; nothing scored)

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--deployment` | `FILE` |  | a deployment/1 file (deploy/&lt;name>.json): its method, model, gates, pair and script — the file `mt-eval run --deployment` tested. Instead of --method / -m / --pair / --gates / --target-script |
| `--method` | `METHOD` |  | lexicon, local-model, or a plugin folder whose method.json declares dependency_class S or O — a method that sends text elsewhere is not served |
| `-m`, `--model` | `MODEL` |  | the dictionary (lexicon) or model (local-model) the method runs |
| `--pair` | `PAIR` |  | Language pair: 'eng>crk' (quoted — an unquoted > is a shell redirect), eng-crk, or 'eng→crk' |
| `--host` | `HOST` |  | default 127.0.0.1 (this machine only, or the deployment's serve.host); another host needs $MT_EVAL_SERVE_TOKEN |
| `--port` | `PORT` |  | default 8379 (or the deployment's serve.port) |
| `--gates` | `FILE` |  | A gate-chain/1 file: every answer is gated before it is sent — a dropped key comes back as an error, keep-source sends the source, flag sends the output and names the key, fallback sends the chain's fallback's translation if the gates accept it |
| `--target-script` | `ISO15924` |  | the script the output is written in (e.g. Cyrl), for a gate that checks it: a server has no references to read it from |
| `--holders-agreed-by` | `WHO` |  | for a method whose output is local-only, served on another host: who among the data's holders agreed that it may leave this machine (reported on /health) |

## `mt-eval compare`

Compare two or more runs

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `report …` | Run reports (\*_report.json, what `mt-eval run` writes beside its run log) or run logs (run_\*.json — the sibling _report.json is used). The first is run A, the second B, … |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-o`, `--output` | `OUTPUT` |  | Where to write the comparison JSON (an existing file there is replaced, and the output says so). Default: comparison-&lt;hash>.json — the hash of the compared runs' ids, so another comparison never overwrites it — beside the reports when they share a folder, else in comparisons/ in their nearest common folder (never one run's own folder; the path is printed). |
| `--significance` | switch |  | Decide which run is better: a paired significance test on corpus chrF++ (the scoring standard's primary metric; it alone decides), with BLEU/spBLEU/TER/COMET tested beside it and diagnostics apart — every pair, each named by its run-table letters; each Δ comes with its 95% CI. Without it, compare shows the numbers and makes no decision |
| `--method` | one of: `approximate_randomization`, `paired_bootstrap` | `approximate_randomization` | The paired test --significance runs: approximate_randomization (default; a true two-sided significance level, SacreBLEU's default) or paired_bootstrap (Koehn 2004 sign-flip heuristic — conservative/biased, for comparison with older papers) |
| `--n-bootstrap` | `N_BOOTSTRAP` | `1000` | Number of resampling iterations (AR trials / bootstrap resamples) for significance testing. Default: 1000 |
| `--show-text` | switch |  | Print corpus sentences even when the corpus is local-only, sealed or consent-required, or the translations come from a local-only model (otherwise ids and scores are printed instead). Only for a human at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider. |

## `mt-eval queue`

Run the top of the community compute queue with your own key

Execute open items from the public queue (champollion.dev/queue.json), which is ranked by expected chain value — mesh improvement per estimated dollar. Items run in queue order; the plan and estimated spend are shown and confirmed before anything is executed. Results are auto-published after each run (pass --no-publish to skip).

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--top` | `N` |  | Run the first N runnable items. |
| `--budget` | `USD` |  | Run items from the top while estimated spend stays within this amount. |
| `--queue` | `QUEUE` | `db` | Queue source: 'db' (live DB via queue_top, the default; falls back to the static blob), or an http(s) URL / local path to a queue.json (default: db) |
| `--include-coached` | switch |  | Allow coached items (requires --coaching-file). |
| `--coaching-file` | `COACHING_FILE` |  | Your coaching file, substituted into coached items' run commands. |
| `--provider` | one of: `openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `local` |  | LLM API provider. Auto-detected from your environment if not specified. (openrouter, openai, anthropic, gemini, local) |
| `--dry-run` | switch |  | Print the plan and exit without running anything. |
| `--stop-on-failure` | switch |  | Abort the batch on the first failing item. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | switch |  | Skip the confirmation prompt (cron use). |
| `--no-publish` | switch |  | Skip auto-publishing after each run. Results can still be published manually later with 'mt-eval publish'. |
| `--anonymous` | switch |  | Publish results WITHOUT signing in — the leaderboard shows submitter 'anonymous'. No account needed; sign in only if you want your name on the board. (Non-interactive runs with no cached sign-in default to this.) |
| `--jobs`, `-j` | `N` |  | Number of queue items to run concurrently (default: 8, or 1 for ≤3 items). Higher values finish faster but may hit API rate limits. |
| `--timeout` | `SECS` | `300` | Per-item timeout in seconds (default: 300). Items exceeding this are killed and skipped. |
| `--spread` | switch |  | Spread selection across a priority band so simultaneous contributors don't all run the same items (default for --budget, the donate flow). |
| `--no-spread` | switch |  | Disable anti-collision spread; take items in strict queue order (default for --top). |
| `--spread-seed` | `N` |  | Seed the spread RNG for reproducible selection (testing/debugging). |

Submit a TestReport to the leaderboard

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--republish-dir` | `DIR` |  | Publish EVERY \*_report.json under DIR (recursive, oldest first) — the one-command recovery for a queue batch whose auto-publishes hit the anonymous rate limit. Already-published runs are skipped (read-only pre-flight, no rate-limit cost); publishing stops honestly when the intake's window is exhausted and reports what remains. No per-report prompts. |
| `--method-card` | `METHOD_CARD` |  | Path to a method card JSON file to attach to the submission |
| `-y`, `--yes` | switch |  | Skip confirmation prompt (required for scripted/batch publishing) |
| `--scores-only`, `--private` | switch |  | Publish ONLY aggregate scores + corpus sha256/size (owner-attested, self-reported). Never uploads the source/reference text — use this for your own or private/confidential corpora. |
| `--publish-entries` | switch |  | Force-upload per-entry corpus content for an UNREGISTERED corpus you hold redistribution rights to. Has no effect on NC / no-deriv / held-out / quarantined corpora (their content is never exposed). |
| `--redact-coaching` | switch |  | Publish with the coaching/system prompt text replaced by a marker (also the way past a refusal when the prompt embeds source+reference pairs of a restricted corpus). The prompt's sha256 provenance is kept; the full text stays in the local RunLog. A local-only corpus's coached prompt is redacted by default. |
| `--dry-run` | switch |  | Assemble and PRINT the run-card payload without writing to the leaderboard (no auth, no network). Preview a publish safely. |
| `--prod`, `--yes-prod` | switch |  | Explicitly authorize a write to the PRODUCTION leaderboard. Without this (or MT_EVAL_ALLOW_PROD=1) a real prod publish is refused — preview with --dry-run first. |
| `--anonymous` | switch |  | Publish WITHOUT signing in — no account needed; the leaderboard shows submitter 'anonymous'. Goes through the anonymous intake (rate-limited per IP; same integrity gates). Sign in only if you want your name on the board. |

## `mt-eval contest`

Sovereign contests: qualify locally, submit a model or method, rank, close

A CONTEST IS SOVEREIGN HOSTING (the rule since 2026-09-06). An entry is not a file of translations and not a link to a score you published yourself: it is a MODEL (weights, `submit-model`) or a METHOD (code, `submit-method`) handed to the organizer's own air-gapped node, which executes it against a sealed set that never leaves that machine and publishes the score it measured itself.

The open leaderboard is a different thing and still works the old way: `mt-eval publish` puts a self-reported card on the public board, indexed by corpus × pair direction. That is not a contest and carries no prize.

```text
THE FLOW (participant, then organizer):
  1. contest qualify      self-score the PUBLIC dev set → a receipt (the admission gate)
  2. contest validate     rehearse the node's own checks on your bundle, offline
  3. contest submit-model / submit-method
                          hand over the entry; declare track, parameters, licence,
                          primary/contrastive — and accept the prize terms if any
  4. node approve         the organizer authorizes the run (custodian gate)
  5. node serve           the node re-runs your qualifier, executes the entry on the
                          sealed set, and publishes (or defers) the card it measured
  6. contest rank         provisional ranking with tie groups; contest close freezes it
```

```text
RETIRED 2026-09-06: `contest submit` — linking a self-reported card.
RETIRED 2026-09-06: `contest submit-hypotheses` — uploading translations.
Neither is a contest entry path any more; both were deleted rather than left as a trap
that fails halfway.
```

Subcommands: [`create`](#mt-eval-contest-create), [`prepare`](#mt-eval-contest-prepare), [`register`](#mt-eval-contest-register), [`qualify`](#mt-eval-contest-qualify), [`validate`](#mt-eval-contest-validate), [`submit-method`](#mt-eval-contest-submit-method), [`submit-model`](#mt-eval-contest-submit-model), [`method-status`](#mt-eval-contest-method-status), [`status`](#mt-eval-contest-status), [`list`](#mt-eval-contest-list), [`submissions`](#mt-eval-contest-submissions), [`open-intake`](#mt-eval-contest-open-intake), [`close-intake`](#mt-eval-contest-close-intake), [`rank`](#mt-eval-contest-rank), [`close`](#mt-eval-contest-close), [`export`](#mt-eval-contest-export), [`select-for-human-eval`](#mt-eval-contest-select-for-human-eval).

### `mt-eval contest create`

Create a new evaluation contest

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | `NAME` |  | **Required.** Contest name (e.g. 'EN→CRK Open') |
| `--slug` | `SLUG` |  | The contest id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Entrants pass it to `contest qualify` / `submit-method`. Default: derived from --name (printed when the contest is created) |
| `--corpus` | `CORPUS` |  | **Required.** Corpus file or dataset ID to evaluate against |
| `--language-pair` | `LANGUAGE_PAIR` |  | **Required.** Language pair: 'eng>crk' (quoted — an unquoted > is a shell redirect), eng-crk, or 'eng→crk'; stored as eng>crk |
| `--visibility` | one of: `public`, `private`, `team` | `public` | Access mode. public: anyone; private: visible but scores hidden; team: invite-only. Default: public |
| `--use-context` | one of: `commercial`, `non-commercial` | `non-commercial` | Whether this contest/prize is a commercial or non-commercial use (migration 035). A non-commercial contest MAY use NonCommercial (CC-BY-NC) datasets; a commercial contest may NOT. Quarantined corpora are never eligible in either lane. Default: non-commercial |
| `--teams` | `TEAMS` |  | Comma-separated team slugs (required for --visibility team) |
| `--description` | `DESCRIPTION` |  | Human-readable contest description |
| `--primary-metric` | `PRIMARY_METRIC` | `chrf_plus_plus` | Metric `contest rank`/`close` rank on, recorded as metadata.primary_metric: chrf_plus_plus (default; the scoring standard's headline) or another rankable metric — chrf_plain \| bleu \| spbleu \| ter \| comet_score \| exact_match_rate (`chrf` means plain chrF). The retired composite is refused for a new contest. Frozen once any entry exists (migration 072). Tiebreaks: chrF++ → BLEU → COMET → earliest submission. |
| `--test-size` | `TEST_SIZE` |  | Segments in the test the contest ranks on — stated with its minimum detectable effect as the frozen metadata.declared_power (power.py) |
| `--power-pilot` | `REPORT_A REPORT_B` |  | Two TestReports of two systems on the PUBLIC dev set (e.g. the official baselines): their paired outputs fit the effect parameters behind the declared minimum detectable effect (metadata.declared_power). Without it only BLEU gets an MDE (the labelled published prior); other metrics state the test size and say why no MDE is given |
| `--metric-model` | `METRIC_MODEL` |  | The neural model a model-scored primary metric (comet_score) uses, e.g. Unbabel/wmt22-comet-da. Required for those; recorded with the harness version as the frozen metadata.metric_signature. |
| `--results-visibility` | one of: `immediate`, `hidden_until_close` | `hidden_until_close` | When scored cards become visible. hidden_until_close (default): every card is withheld (contest_deferred_results) and published by `contest close` before the ranking freezes — no feedback from the sealed set while the contest runs, so nobody can tune against it. immediate: each card publishes as the node finishes it (a live board). A PROMISE: frozen once the contest has entries (migration 074). |
| `--anonymize-until-close` | switch |  | Pseudonymise entrants in the ORGANIZER'S ranking artifacts while the contest is open (revealed by `contest close`). This does NOT anonymise the public board — a published run card shows whatever run_cards shows. Use --results-visibility hidden_until_close to actually hide results. |
| `--prize-disposition` | one of: `pass_to_holders`, `retain_ip`, `release_open` |  | Declare this contest's prize terms as ONE choice of three. pass_to_holders: the method passes to the sovereign benchmark holders — they score it and keep it, regardless of who wins. retain_ip: you keep ownership of your method — the host scores it and keeps at most a sealed copy for audit. release_open: you keep ownership but must publish the method under an open licence — that release is the prize condition. The chosen term is printed in plain language with its SHA-256 before anything is written; that hash is what entrants pass to --accept-terms. A contest with NO declared term has no prize — that is the default and it is not a lesser contest |
| `--prize-terms` | `JSON-FILE` |  | Declare the same thing from a JSON file: {"disposition": "pass_to_holders"\|"retain_ip"\|"release_open"} plus only the overrides that disposition allows. Mutually exclusive with --prize-disposition, and checked the same way, so a term the chosen option does not offer is refused here, at declaration time, not at ranking time |
| `--prize-retention` | one of: `retain_sealed_audit`, `delete_after_scoring` |  | retain_ip ONLY: what the host keeps. Default retain_sealed_audit (a sealed copy, for audit and reproduction of this result); delete_after_scoring destroys the artifact once it has been scored. Refused on any other option — what the host keeps follows from the term |
| `--prize-release-timing` | one of: `required_before_scores`, `required_before_prize`, `required_after_prize` |  | release_open ONLY: when the public release falls due. Default required_before_prize; required_before_scores holds the entrant's scores until they publish; required_after_prize falls due AFTER payout and is therefore not one of the checks made before paying |
| `--prize-release-license` | `SPDX` |  | release_open ONLY: the licence the entrant must publish under — an SPDX identifier (Apache-2.0, MIT, AGPL-3.0-or-later) or any_osi for any OSI-approved licence (the default) |
| `--prize-terms-url` | `URL` |  | Optional on any option: an https:// link to the host's own written terms, shown to entrants alongside the declared term and covered by its hash |

### `mt-eval contest prepare`

Split a master corpus into the PUBLIC dev set (the qualifier entrants self-score on), the SEALED secret set your node executes handed-over entries against, and an optional second sealed holdout; seal them at rest and register the contest — champollion.dev/docs/network/sovereignty/run-a-sovereign-contest

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--corpus` | `CORPUS` |  | **Required.** Master corpus file (harness JSON/JSONL/TSV). Stays local. |
| `--slug` | `SLUG` |  | **Required.** The contest id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. 'eng-crk-open-2026'). It is the id entrants pass to `contest qualify` / `submit-method`, the key of the node's config, and part of every sealed-set and qualifier id |
| `--name` | `NAME` |  | **Required.** Human-readable contest name |
| `--pair` | `PAIR` |  | **Required.** ISO 639-3 pair: 'eng>crk' (quoted — an unquoted > is a shell redirect), eng-crk, or 'eng→crk' |
| `--dev-size` | `DEV_SIZE` |  | **Required.** Entries in the public dev set (the qualifier) |
| `--blind-size` | `BLIND_SIZE` | `0` | Entries in the OPTIONAL blind set (source released, refs withheld). Default 0: since 2026-09-06 the blind tier is no longer a contest entry path; it survives only as an organizer diagnostic round. |
| `--secret-size` | `SECRET_SIZE` | `0` | Entries in the T2 fully-secret set the node executes handed-over methods against — the contest's own corpus under R2 (default 0) |
| `--sealed-holdout-size` | `SEALED_HOLDOUT_SIZE` | `0` | Entries in a SECOND sealed holdout split (default 0: none). Sealed like the secret set, registered as its own sealed set, named on the contest as metadata.sealed_holdout_set_id, executed inside the SAME authorized run, and always withheld until the contest closes. Needs --secret-size. |
| `--test-suite` | `CORPUS-CARD-ID[=PATH]` |  | Declare a THIRD-PARTY public diagnostic suite every entry is also run on (repeatable). Must be a registered, non-quarantined, sha-pinned public corpus card for this contest's pair, and never one of the contest's own splits. Recorded as metadata.test_suites and frozen once entries exist; reported, never ranked. Prepare warns, with counts, when a sealed row also appears in a suite (or in the released dev set); =PATH names your local copy of the suite for that check (its sha256 must match the pin), else a copy already on this machine is used (prepare downloads nothing) and a suite with no local copy is reported as unchecked. |
| `--seed` | `SEED` |  | **Required.** Split seed — REQUIRED so the split is deterministic and auditable |
| `--qualifier-threshold` | `QUALIFIER_THRESHOLD` |  | **Required.** The score a method must reach on the public dev set before your node runs it on the sealed set (and the sealed holdout, if any). On the 0-100 chrF++ scale: the qualifier score is corpus chrF++ (sacreBLEU, word_order=2) on the dev set — the scoring standard's headline, nothing blended in. REQUIRED — thresholds are contest data, never a code default. |
| `--authorization-model` | one of: `per-submission`, `blanket`, `open` |  | Authorization posture: per-submission (custodian approves each scoring; DEFAULT, fail-closed), blanket (qualifier pass auto-authorizes, full audit trail), open (direct). Unset + --shared-task: the edition's default applies |
| `--intake-daily-limit` | `INTAKE_DAILY_LIMIT` |  | Max submissions per participant per 24h (anti-probing; default 5, or the edition's default with --shared-task) |
| `--shared-task` | `SHARED_TASK` |  | Attach this per-pair contest to a multi-pair shared-task edition (`mt-eval shared-task create`), e.g. 'example-task-2026'. Grouping + policy defaults only — every gate stays per-contest (migration 046) |
| `--custodian-group` | `CUSTODIAN_GROUP` |  | OPAQUE custodian group id (never a real org name pre-consent). Required unless --plaintext-refs. |
| `--threshold-pubkey` | `THRESHOLD_PUBKEY` |  | Sealing public key (file/base64; `champollion network seal-corpus keygen`). Required unless --plaintext-refs. |
| `--plaintext-refs` | switch |  | Keep refs unencrypted on disk (refused for per-submission authorization — see runbook) |
| `--license` | `LICENSE` |  | REQUIRED. Licence the RELEASED files (dev set + blind source) are offered under, as the rights-holder grants it (SPDX id, e.g. CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, or LicenseRef-&lt;terms>). Never defaulted: it gates every entrant's run |
| `--do-not-train` | one of: `true`, `false` |  | The training term the RELEASED files state (dataset.do_not_train). Read from the master's own card first; use this when the card does not say. It can tighten the master's term, never loosen it |
| `--year` | `YEAR` |  | Qualifier vintage year (default: current year) |
| `--out` | `OUT` |  | **Required.** Output dir (public/ = releasable, local/ = organizer-only; run logs and caches go to runs/) |
| `--visibility` | one of: `public`, `private`, `team` |  | Who can see the contest. Default: public. Not frozen by the database (no mt-eval command changes it after registration) |
| `--use-context` | one of: `commercial`, `non-commercial` |  | The use the contest is for; the corpus licence must allow it. Default: non-commercial. FIXED AT REGISTRATION: part of the contest's identity, which the database never lets change (migration 072) |
| `--description` | `DESCRIPTION` |  | Public description of the contest. Default: none |
| `--no-register` | switch |  | Write artifacts only; print the registration plan instead of touching Supabase |
| `--closed-intake` | switch |  | Register with intake_open=false (open it later) |
| `--self-serve` | switch |  | Register with YOUR OWN sign-in instead of the service key (migration 046 — shared-task organizer onboarding). Rows are identity-bound to your JWT email; no MT_EVAL_SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY needed. |
| `--primary-metric` | `PRIMARY_METRIC` |  | Metric `contest rank`/`close` rank on (metadata.primary_metric): chrf_plus_plus (default; the scoring standard's headline) or another rankable metric — chrf_plain \| bleu \| spbleu \| ter \| comet_score \| exact_match_rate. The retired composite is refused for a new contest. Frozen once the contest has its first entry (migration 072) |
| `--power-pilot` | `REPORT_A REPORT_B` |  | Two TestReports of two systems on the PUBLIC dev set (e.g. the official baselines): their paired outputs fit the effect parameters behind the declared minimum detectable effect (metadata.declared_power). Without it only BLEU gets an MDE (the labelled published prior); other metrics state the test size and say why no MDE is given |
| `--metric-model` | `METRIC_MODEL` |  | The neural model a model-scored primary metric (comet_score) uses, e.g. Unbabel/wmt22-comet-da. Required for those; recorded with the harness version as the frozen metadata.metric_signature. |
| `--results-visibility` | one of: `immediate`, `hidden_until_close` |  | When scored cards become visible. hidden_until_close (default): every card is withheld (contest_deferred_results) and published by `contest close` before the ranking freezes — no feedback from the sealed set while the contest runs, so nobody can tune against it. immediate: each card publishes as the node finishes it (a live board). A PROMISE: frozen once the contest has entries (migration 074) |
| `--anonymize-until-close` | switch |  | Pseudonymise entrants in the ORGANIZER'S ranking artifacts while the contest is open (revealed by `contest close`). This does NOT anonymise the public board — a published run card shows whatever run_cards shows. Default: off. A PROMISE: frozen once the contest has entries (migration 074) |
| `--prize-disposition` | one of: `pass_to_holders`, `retain_ip`, `release_open` |  | Declare this contest's prize terms as ONE choice of three. pass_to_holders: the method passes to the sovereign benchmark holders — they score it and keep it, regardless of who wins. retain_ip: you keep ownership of your method — the host scores it and keeps at most a sealed copy for audit. release_open: you keep ownership but must publish the method under an open licence — that release is the prize condition. The chosen term is printed in plain language with its SHA-256 before anything is written; that hash is what entrants pass to --accept-terms. A contest with NO declared term has no prize — that is the default and it is not a lesser contest |
| `--prize-terms` | `JSON-FILE` |  | Declare the same thing from a JSON file: {"disposition": "pass_to_holders"\|"retain_ip"\|"release_open"} plus only the overrides that disposition allows. Mutually exclusive with --prize-disposition, and checked the same way, so a term the chosen option does not offer is refused here, at declaration time, not at ranking time |
| `--prize-retention` | one of: `retain_sealed_audit`, `delete_after_scoring` |  | retain_ip ONLY: what the host keeps. Default retain_sealed_audit (a sealed copy, for audit and reproduction of this result); delete_after_scoring destroys the artifact once it has been scored. Refused on any other option — what the host keeps follows from the term |
| `--prize-release-timing` | one of: `required_before_scores`, `required_before_prize`, `required_after_prize` |  | release_open ONLY: when the public release falls due. Default required_before_prize; required_before_scores holds the entrant's scores until they publish; required_after_prize falls due AFTER payout and is therefore not one of the checks made before paying |
| `--prize-release-license` | `SPDX` |  | release_open ONLY: the licence the entrant must publish under — an SPDX identifier (Apache-2.0, MIT, AGPL-3.0-or-later) or any_osi for any OSI-approved licence (the default) |
| `--prize-terms-url` | `URL` |  | Optional on any option: an https:// link to the host's own written terms, shown to entrants alongside the declared term and covered by its hash |

### `mt-eval contest qualify`

Self-score your system on a contest's PUBLIC dev set and write the qualifier receipt that submit-model/submit-method require

The qualifier score is corpus chrF++ (sacreBLEU, word_order=2) on the 0-100 scale — the scoring standard's headline, with nothing blended in. The organizer's node computes the same number when it re-runs your method. qualify reads the contest's qualifier id and threshold from the contest database; with --offline-qualifier-id and --offline-threshold (both published with the dev release) it touches no network at all.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `contest_id` | Contest id — the --slug given to `contest prepare` (`mt-eval contest list` shows it) |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dev` | `DEV` |  | **Required.** Your translations of the PUBLIC dev set: one per line in corpus order, id-keyed JSON, or the run log `mt-eval run --corpus <dev corpus>` wrote (or its _report.json) as it is — read by entry id, and checked to be a run on this dev corpus |
| `--dev-corpus` | `DEV_CORPUS` |  | **Required.** The released public dev corpus file (source+refs) — its dataset.corpus_id must BE the qualifier's |
| `--system` | `SYSTEM` |  | **Required.** Your system's name. Recorded on the receipt, and the receipt is kept per contest AND system, so qualifying a second system never replaces the first; re-qualifying the same system keeps the previous receipt under history/. `submit-method` / `submit-model --system` pick it |
| `--method-class` | one of: `raw-llm`, `coached-llm`, `pipeline`, `custom-plugin`, `api`, `human` |  | **Required.** Claimed method class (method-card vocabulary) |
| `--paradigm` | one of: `rule-based`, `statistical`, `neural-nmt`, `llm`, `hybrid`, `human`, `unknown` |  | Claimed paradigm (default: unknown) |
| `--receipt-dir` | `RECEIPT_DIR` |  | Where to write the receipt (default ~/.mt-eval/qualifier/&lt;contest-id>/&lt;system>-&lt;hash>.json) |
| `--offline-threshold` | `OFFLINE_THRESHOLD` |  | Fully offline: the organizer-published threshold, on the 0-100 chrF++ qualifier scale (with --offline-qualifier-id; no network at all) |
| `--offline-qualifier-id` | `OFFLINE_QUALIFIER_ID` |  | Fully offline: the organizer-published qualifier id (required with --offline-threshold) |

### `mt-eval contest validate`

Pre-flight your entry OFFLINE: run the node's static checks on a bundle (or model dir) and, with --dev, the dev-set alignment and self-score. A rehearsal — the node re-executes

Run, locally and offline, exactly the checks the organizer's node runs FIRST: the lane's static checks (Lane B sandbox or Lane A declarative), and — with --dev/--dev-corpus — that your dev hypotheses line up with the released dev corpus plus the self-score, checked against the qualifier receipt submit-method / submit-model will use (validate writes no receipt — `contest qualify` does). This is a REHEARSAL: the node re-executes your bundle itself and re-runs the qualifier on its own copy of the dev set, and its measurement is the one that gates. Exit 0 means zero BLOCK findings — never that the run will score.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `path` | The bundle .tar.gz your submit command wrote, a bundle directory (one containing manifest.json), or a source directory with --manifest |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--lane` | one of: `method`, `model` |  | Force the lane (default: inferred — a Dockerfile is Lane B, manifest.model.weightsFile is Lane A) |
| `--manifest` | `MANIFEST` |  | Pack a SOURCE directory with this manifest.json first, so what is checked is byte-for-byte what would be submitted |
| `--method-dir` | `METHOD_DIR` | `method` | Lane B, with --manifest: the code directory inside the source dir (default: method) |
| `--dockerfile` | `DOCKERFILE` | `Dockerfile` | Lane B, with --manifest: the Dockerfile inside the source dir (default: Dockerfile) |
| `--secret-set` | `SECRET_SET` |  | The sealed set id the bundle targets — checked against the manifest's declared corpus id |
| `--contest` | `CONTEST` |  | Contest id — the --slug given to `contest prepare` (required with --dev; your receipt is looked up under it) |
| `--dev` | `DEV` |  | Your translations of the PUBLIC dev set (one per line, id-keyed JSON, or an `mt-eval run` run log of the dev corpus) — turns on the qualifier rehearsal (alignment + self-score) |
| `--dev-corpus` | `DEV_CORPUS` |  | The released public dev corpus file (source+refs) |
| `--system` | `SYSTEM` |  | The system your qualifier receipt was written for (`contest qualify --system`). A packed bundle carries the receipt it was packaged with, and that is the one checked (validate finds it on this machine and names its system; a --system naming another receipt is a warning). For a source directory packed here with --manifest: the receipt submit will embed (default: the one named like the manifest's method, else the contest's only receipt) |
| `--method-class` | one of: `raw-llm`, `coached-llm`, `pipeline`, `custom-plugin`, `api`, `human` |  | Method class for the self-score (default: the manifest's) |
| `--paradigm` | one of: `rule-based`, `statistical`, `neural-nmt`, `llm`, `hybrid`, `human`, `unknown` |  | Paradigm for the self-score (default: the manifest's) |
| `--offline-qualifier-id` | `OFFLINE_QUALIFIER_ID` |  | The organizer-published qualifier id (default: the one the bundle's own receipt names) |
| `--offline-threshold` | `OFFLINE_THRESHOLD` |  | The organizer-published threshold, on the 0-100 chrF++ qualifier scale (default: the one the bundle's own receipt names) |
| `--receipt-dir` | `RECEIPT_DIR` |  | Where your qualifier receipts are (default ~/.mt-eval/qualifier/&lt;contest-id>/&lt;system>-&lt;hash>.json — one per system). Read only: validate writes no receipt |
| `--json` | switch |  | Machine-readable result on stdout (findings, counts, ok) — banners go to stderr |

### `mt-eval contest submit-method`

Lane B — hand a RUNNABLE method bundle (code) to the organizer's air-gapped node for execution against the contest's sealed set: static pre-flight → deterministic tarball → authorization request (sandbox-evaluation-spec §2). Admission is your PASSING `contest qualify` receipt on the public dev set, which the node re-executes on its own copy before any grant is minted

Every submission needs: --method-dir, --dockerfile, --name, --version, --entrypoint, --method-class, --developer, --node-id, --agree, a passing `mt-eval contest qualify` receipt, and the declarations --track and --parameter-count. With --parameter-count above 0 also --weights-license and one of --weights-public/--weights-private; a method with no trained weights passes --parameter-count 0 and neither. --track constrained also needs --training-data-file. --offline also needs --bundle-out, --secret-set, --pair, --developer-email, --offline-qualifier-id and --offline-threshold. A contest that declares prize terms needs --accept-terms; one that sets require_description needs --description-file.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `contest_id` | Contest id — the --slug given to `contest prepare` (`mt-eval contest list` shows it) |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--method-dir` | `METHOD_DIR` |  | **Required.** Directory with your method's code/weights/config. Packed as method/ in the bundle and mounted read-only at /method on the node, so &lt;method-dir>/translate.py runs as /method/translate.py |
| `--dockerfile` | `DOCKERFILE` |  | **Required.** Dockerfile that builds WITHOUT network access (all dependencies vendored — spec §3.3) |
| `--name` | `NAME` |  | **Required.** Method name |
| `--version` | `VERSION` |  | **Required.** Method version |
| `--entrypoint` | `ENTRYPOINT` |  | **Required.** The script the node runs (stdin sources → stdout translations, spec §2.2), as its path inside --method-dir, e.g. translate.py for &lt;method-dir>/translate.py. Its bundle path (method/translate.py) is accepted too; an ambiguous name is refused with both readings |
| `--method-class` | one of: `raw-llm`, `coached-llm`, `pipeline`, `custom-plugin`, `api`, `human` |  | **Required.** Method class (method-card vocabulary; execution-verified in this lane) |
| `--paradigm` | one of: `rule-based`, `statistical`, `neural-nmt`, `llm`, `hybrid`, `human`, `unknown` |  | Paradigm (default: unknown) |
| `--description` | `DESCRIPTION` |  | One-line method description |
| `--developer` | `DEVELOPER` |  | **Required.** Developer name (manifest.developer.name) |
| `--developer-email` | `DEVELOPER_EMAIL` |  | Only for --offline; online it must match your login identity |
| `--affiliation` | `AFFILIATION` |  | Affiliation |
| `--agree` | switch |  | REQUIRED: you have read and agree to the method-submission terms framework (https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/legal/method-submission-agreement.md) |
| `--node-id` | `NODE_ID` |  | **Required.** The ORGANIZER-ADVERTISED scoring node id — the request fingerprint binds your method to it |
| `--corpus-version` | `CORPUS_VERSION` | `v1` | Sealed corpus version (organizer-advertised; default v1) |
| `--secret-set` | `SECRET_SET` |  | Sealed set id (auto-resolved from the contest when unambiguous; required with --offline) |
| `--pair` | `PAIR` |  | Language pair: 'eng>crk' (quoted — an unquoted > is a shell redirect) or eng-crk (only for --offline; online it comes from the contest) |
| `--bundle-out` | `BUNDLE_OUT` |  | Also write a sneakernet exchange dir for true-airgap contests (mt-eval node import-bundle) |
| `--offline` | switch |  | No network at all: package + --bundle-out only |
| `--ram-gb` | `RAM_GB` | `4` | RAM your method needs, GB (default 4, what the shipped `node init` template allows). The node refuses a bundle that exceeds its sandbox.max_ram_gb — if the organizer's node allows more and your method needs it, say so here |
| `--disk-gb` | `DISK_GB` | `4` | Scratch disk your method needs, GB (default 4, the template's sandbox.max_tmp_gb) |
| `--max-runtime-minutes` | `MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES` | `30` | Wall-clock budget your method needs, minutes (default 30, the template's sandbox.max_runtime_minutes); the node refuses more than its sandbox.max_runtime_minutes |
| `--gpu` | switch |  | Declare that the method needs a GPU. A node without one refuses the bundle rather than running it slowly and calling the result a score |
| `--gpu-memory-gb` | `GPU_MEMORY_GB` | `0` | GPU memory the method needs, GB (with --gpu) |
| `--track` | one of: `constrained`, `unconstrained` |  | **Required.** REQUIRED declaration: 'constrained' = trained only on the data the organizer declared allowed (needs --training-data-file); 'unconstrained' = anything. Ranked in separate partitions. Recorded as your claim — there is no default and nothing infers it for you |
| `--parameter-count` | `PARAMETER_COUNT` |  | **Required.** REQUIRED declaration: total trainable parameters of the system you are entering. In this code lane it is recorded as your claim (nothing can check it). In the Lane A model lane the count is the one the weights FILE stores — the sum of tensor sizes in the safetensors header — which can differ from a count taken in torch (tied weights stored once, tables not saved). Pass 0 for a method with no trained weights (rule-based, dictionary, FST): it then declares no weights licence or openness. A method that prompts an LLM counts the parameters of every model the bundle runs, the LLM included (with the LLM's licence as --weights-license); one calling a hosted LLM cannot enter (no network on the node) |
| `--weights-license` | `WEIGHTS_LICENSE` |  | REQUIRED when --parameter-count is above 0: the licence of the weights your method uses — an SPDX id (Apache-2.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, …) or a LicenseRef-… name. Recorded as your claim; it is what a prize or reuse conversation starts from. Leave it out with --parameter-count 0 (no weights) |
| `--weights-public` | switch |  | One of --weights-public/--weights-private is REQUIRED when --parameter-count is above 0: the weights are publicly downloadable. Recorded as your claim |
| `--weights-private` | switch |  | The weights are not public. Recorded as your claim |
| `--training-data-file` | `TRAINING_DATA_FILE` |  | Path to a plain-text list of the corpora you trained on (≤2000 chars). REQUIRED with --track constrained — the track claim means nothing without the data list it is a claim about |
| `--primary` | switch |  | This is your team's PRIMARY entry (default). Exactly one primary per team is ranked for the win |
| `--contrastive` | switch |  | This is a contrastive entry: scored and reported in its own section, never a winner |
| `--description-file` | `DESCRIPTION_FILE` |  | Path to your system description (≤4000 chars) — how the system was built, in your own words. REQUIRED when the contest sets require_description |
| `--method-release-url` | `METHOD_RELEASE_URL` |  | Optional https:// URL where the method is publicly released. Public information recorded on the submission; it is never a condition of ranking |
| `--accept-terms` | `SHA256` |  | Accept this contest's declared PRIZE TERMS by their SHA-256 hash. REQUIRED when the contest declares any: the contest declares ONE of three options — pass to holders, retain IP, or release open — which settles who keeps the method and whether you must publish it, so nothing is assumed on your behalf. Run without it once and the terms are printed in plain language with the hash to pass back. Your acceptance is packed into the bundle and covered by method_sha, and the organizer's node refuses a bundle that accepted anything else |
| `--receipt-dir` | `RECEIPT_DIR` |  | Where to read the qualifier receipt from (default ~/.mt-eval/qualifier/&lt;contest-id>/, one receipt per system). A PASSING receipt from `mt-eval contest qualify` is required; the node re-executes your bundle on the same public dev set and denies on a miss |
| `--system` | `SYSTEM` |  | Which system's qualifier receipt this submission uses: the name given to `contest qualify --system`. Default: the receipt for --name, else the contest's only receipt; several and none matching is refused with the list |
| `--offline-threshold` | `OFFLINE_THRESHOLD` |  | REQUIRED with --offline: the qualifier threshold the organizer published, on the 0-100 chrF++ qualifier scale (offline there is nothing to look it up against) |
| `--offline-qualifier-id` | `OFFLINE_QUALIFIER_ID` |  | REQUIRED with --offline: the qualifier id the organizer published; it must match your receipt |

### `mt-eval contest submit-model`

Propose a DECLARATIVE neural-MT model (safetensors weights + declarative tokenizer + config) against a contest's secret set. No Dockerfile, no code: the organizer runs the weights in its own trusted engine, so the submission is validated code-free (model_runner.py). The safer, preferred lane for standard NMT.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `contest_id` | Contest id — the --slug given to `contest prepare` (`mt-eval contest list` shows it) |

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--model-dir` | `MODEL_DIR` |  | **Required.** Directory with config.json + model.safetensors + tokenizer files at its ROOT (from_pretrained shape) |
| `--name` | `NAME` |  | **Required.** Model name |
| `--version` | `VERSION` |  | **Required.** Model version |
| `--architecture` | `ARCHITECTURE` |  | **Required.** The model architecture (any architecture the organizer's engine implements natively — e.g. MarianMTModel, M2M100ForConditionalGeneration, MBart/T5/Pegasus/… — hosts are PERMISSIVE by default; a careful host may pin an allowlist) |
| `--method-class` | one of: `raw-llm`, `coached-llm`, `pipeline`, `custom-plugin`, `api`, `human` |  | **Required.** Method class (method-card vocabulary) |
| `--paradigm` | one of: `neural-nmt` | `neural-nmt` | Only neural-nmt runs declaratively (default) |
| `--description` | `DESCRIPTION` |  | One-line model description |
| `--developer` | `DEVELOPER` |  | **Required.** Developer name |
| `--developer-email` | `DEVELOPER_EMAIL` |  | Only for --offline; online it must match your login |
| `--affiliation` | `AFFILIATION` |  | Affiliation |
| `--agree` | switch |  | REQUIRED: you agree to the method-submission terms |
| `--node-id` | `NODE_ID` |  | **Required.** The ORGANIZER-ADVERTISED scoring node id |
| `--corpus-version` | `CORPUS_VERSION` | `v1` | Sealed corpus version (default v1) |
| `--secret-set` | `SECRET_SET` |  | Sealed set id (required with --offline) |
| `--pair` | `PAIR` |  | Language pair: 'eng>crk' (quoted — an unquoted > is a shell redirect) or eng-crk (--offline) |
| `--weights-file` | `WEIGHTS_FILE` | `model.safetensors` | Weights filename in the bundle (default model.safetensors; MUST be safetensors) |
| `--config-file` | `CONFIG_FILE` | `config.json` | Config filename (default config.json) |
| `--src-lang-token` | `SRC_LANG_TOKEN` |  | Tokenizer source language code (NLLB/M2M-style) |
| `--tgt-lang-token` | `TGT_LANG_TOKEN` |  | Tokenizer target language code (forced BOS) |
| `--bundle-out` | `BUNDLE_OUT` |  | Also write a sneakernet exchange dir |
| `--offline` | switch |  | No network at all: package + --bundle-out only |
| `--track` | one of: `constrained`, `unconstrained` |  | **Required.** REQUIRED declaration: 'constrained' = trained only on the data the organizer declared allowed; 'unconstrained' = anything. Ranked in separate partitions. Recorded as your claim — there is no default and nothing infers it for you |
| `--parameter-count` | `PARAMETER_COUNT` |  | **Required.** REQUIRED declaration: total parameters of the submitted model, COUNTED THE WAY THE WEIGHTS FILE STORES THEM — the sum of tensor sizes in the safetensors header (--weights-file). THIS lane checks it: a claim off by more than 1% is refused before upload and again on the node. A count taken in torch (sum(p.numel() …)) can differ: a tied or shared weight is stored once, and a table the model rebuilds at load (e.g. sinusoidal positions) may not be saved. A refusal prints the file's count — declare that |
| `--weights-license` | `WEIGHTS_LICENSE` |  | **Required.** REQUIRED declaration: the licence of these weights — an SPDX id (Apache-2.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, …) or a LicenseRef-… name. Recorded as your claim |
| `--weights-public` | switch |  | REQUIRED (with --weights-private): the weights are publicly downloadable. Recorded as your claim |
| `--weights-private` | switch |  | The weights are not public. Recorded as your claim |
| `--training-data-file` | `TRAINING_DATA_FILE` |  | Path to a plain-text list of the corpora you trained on (≤2000 chars). REQUIRED with --track constrained — the track claim means nothing without the data list it is a claim about |
| `--primary` | switch |  | This is your team's PRIMARY entry (default). Exactly one primary per team is ranked for the win |
| `--contrastive` | switch |  | This is a contrastive entry: scored and reported in its own section, never a winner |
| `--description-file` | `DESCRIPTION_FILE` |  | Path to your system description (≤4000 chars) — how the model was built, in your own words. REQUIRED when the contest sets require_description |
| `--method-release-url` | `METHOD_RELEASE_URL` |  | Optional https:// URL where the model is publicly released. Public information recorded on the submission; it is never a condition of ranking |
| `--accept-terms` | `SHA256` |  | Accept this contest's declared PRIZE TERMS by their SHA-256 hash. REQUIRED when the contest declares any: the contest declares ONE of three options — pass to holders, retain IP, or release open — which settles who keeps the model and whether you must publish it, so nothing is assumed on your behalf. Run without it once and the terms are printed in plain language with the hash to pass back. Your acceptance is packed into the bundle and covered by method_sha, and the organizer's node refuses a bundle that accepted anything else |
| `--receipt-dir` | `RECEIPT_DIR` |  | Where to read the qualifier receipt from (default ~/.mt-eval/qualifier/&lt;contest-id>/, one receipt per system). A PASSING receipt from `mt-eval contest qualify` is required; the node re-executes your model on the same public dev set and denies on a miss |
| `--system` | `SYSTEM` |  | Which system's qualifier receipt this submission uses: the name given to `contest qualify --system`. Default: the receipt for --name, else the contest's only receipt; several and none matching is refused with the list |
| `--offline-threshold` | `OFFLINE_THRESHOLD` |  | REQUIRED with --offline: the qualifier threshold the organizer published, on the 0-100 chrF++ qualifier scale (offline there is nothing to look it up against) |
| `--offline-qualifier-id` | `OFFLINE_QUALIFIER_ID` |  | REQUIRED with --offline: the qualifier id the organizer published; it must match your receipt |
